newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's reserves fell in June due to debt payment.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's reserves fell in June due to debt payment.

text.p: Brazil's foreign reserves fell about $1.7 billion in June, largely due to interest and principal payments on foreign debt, a Central Bank official said Monday.

Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, said routine Central Bank operations in the foreign currency markets also ate away at some of the reserves, which dropped to $56.8 billion in June from $58.5 billion the month before.
"They are already recovering this month (July)," Lopes said.
He listed the following foreign currency outflows and inflows:
-- In the foreign exchange markets, the Central Bank spent a net $1.125 billion.
-- Brazil paid $538 million to the Paris Club of debtor nations, of which $245 million was principal and $293 million interest.
-- Brazil paid $728 million to retire a two-year Samurai bond that came due in June, of which $41 million was interest and $687 million principal.
-- Brazil paid $807 million on an Interest Due Unpaid (IDU) bond, making good on a default. Of that, $606 million was principal payment and $201 million interest.
-- On the inflow side, Brazil had $705 million come in from its 30-year global bond.
-- It also freed up $620 million in collateral from retired Brady Bonds swapped for the global or bought in a buyback operation linked to the global.
-- In other operations, Brazil gained $209 million.
The inflows and outflows resulted in a net reduction in foreign reserves of $1.664 billion, Lopes said.
